title: Grafana Tempo 3.1 Adds Query-Based Trace Redaction and Sampling-Aware TraceQL Metrics
gist: Grafana Labs released Tempo 3.1, the first minor update to the Kafka-based 3.0 architecture, adding Kafka TLS/SASL support, TraceQL-based trace redaction, and sampling-aware TraceQL metrics, with simple metrics queries running close to twice as fast.

insights.claim: Grafana Tempo 3.0, published in June, made the Kafka-compatible architecture (Project Rhythm) the default for microservices deployments, replacing ingesters and compactors with block-builders, live-stores, a backend scheduler and workers.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Tempo operators now run Kafka on the critical path of tracing, shifting operational and cost considerations toward Kafka.

insights.claim: Grafana says dropping replication factor 3 in Tempo's new design cuts storage from 3 to 3.5 times the trace volume down to a single copy.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Roughly 3x lower trace storage cost is a strong incentive for self-hosted Tempo users to migrate to 3.x.

insights.claim: Tempo 3.0's Kafka client supported only SASL PLAIN over an unencrypted connection, so any broker requiring TLS refused it; 3.1 adds TLS (including optional mTLS), SCRAM-SHA-256/512, OAUTHBEARER and AWS_MSK_IAM.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Managed Kafka services such as AWS MSK become viable backends for Tempo, widening enterprise adoption.
insights.locator: Because Kafka is now on the critical path

insights.claim: A new client_rack option enables rack-aware fetching (KIP-392) so Tempo components read from a replica in their own availability zone and avoid cross-zone transfer charges, provided brokers have rack IDs configured.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Cross-AZ data transfer is a real cloud cost line for observability; this feature reduces it.

insights.claim: A new producer_compression option (none, gzip, snappy, lz4, zstd; default snappy) together with TLS makes Azure Event Hubs usable as a Tempo backend because it accepts only gzip, and all three Kafka changes came from community contributors.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Support for Azure's Kafka-compatible service opens Tempo 3.x to Azure-centric shops; community contribution signals healthy open-source momentum.

insights.claim: Tempo 3.1's tempo-cli redact now accepts a TraceQL query (with a --dry-run mode) instead of an enumerated list of trace IDs, because sensitive values such as tokens or account numbers often appear in more traces than can practically be listed.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Practical PII/secret scrubbing of stored traces eases compliance workflows for tracing platforms.

insights.claim: Redaction queries are limited to one spanset filter with equality comparisons on resource and span attributes because the rewrite is irreversible, and the --start/--end flags should only be used once all schedulers and workers run 3.1, since older workers ignore the window and remove every match without an error.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Mixed-version clusters risk silent over-deletion of trace data; upgrade all components before using the time-bounded redaction.
insights.locator: Grafana limits the syntax to one spanset filter

insights.claim: An experimental hint, with (extrapolate=true), scales TraceQL metrics by the sampling rate stored in tracestate following OpenTelemetry probability sampling rules, so at 50% sampling each stored span counts as two and spans without a recorded rate count as one.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Sampled tracing can now yield approximately correct rate and count metrics, reducing the need to store unsampled data.
insights.locator: TraceQL metrics, which became generally available in 3.0

insights.claim: The extrapolation hint applies to rate, count_over_time, sum_over_time, avg_over_time, histogram_over_time, quantile_over_time and compare but not min_over_time or max_over_time, and requires vParquet4 or later.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Extrema cannot be corrected for sampling; do not rely on min/max metrics with sampled traces.

insights.claim: Tempo 3.1 makes vParquet5 the default block format and turns on the span-only fetch path by default for vParquet5 blocks; Grafana says simple metrics queries run close to twice as fast, with one warmed-up { } | rate() test finishing in slightly over half the time.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Performance gains of about 2x on metrics queries reduce compute needed for trace-derived metrics; results are from a vendor test.

insights.claim: Tempo adds an experimental POST /api/v2/traces/diff endpoint that compares two traces and can return a compact summary instead of a span-level patch, exposed through the Tempo MCP server, with Grafana saying the smaller payload helps LLM-driven investigations.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Observability vendors are shaping APIs for AI agents (compact payloads, MCP servers), a direction for AIOps product competition.

insights.claim: An experimental span pruning option on the trace-by-ID v2 endpoint collapses similar leaf spans into one summary span carrying count and duration statistics, and the endpoint gains TraceQL filtering.
insights.speaker: Claudio Masolo
insights.so_what: Smaller trace payloads reduce UI and LLM token load for large traces.
insights.locator: Other additions include an experimental span pruning option
